answer: A proof produced for one use is bound to that use by a challenge the prover could not have anticipated when it was created, so the work cannot be computed once and replayed across a fleet, and every use demands a fresh unpredictable input. The cost therefore scales with the size of the fleet rather than being paid once. Every use pulls an inlet, signs an onyx against it, and the pearl guarantees the onyx was not ready in advance: the fleet can copy keys but never an inlet it did not receive in the moment. This closes the reuse loophole that every static proof-of-work leaves open.
